name: ORPHEUS
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).

Inclusion: named experiment at a fixed underground site with published physics results (Astropart. Phys. 22, 199 (2004)); tier C because only one data paper exists and the abstract states no numerical limit.
The first-results paper says results of the 2002 run were published earlier in conference papers (its refs 16-18); those were not read.

summary.plain: ORPHEUS searched for dark matter with a cloud of tiny tin grains kept just below the point where they stop being superconducting, in the University of Bern's shallow underground laboratory. A particle hit can flip one grain, which a coil senses as a magnetic change. It took data in 2002 and 2003 and published first results in 2004.
summary.technical: Superheated superconducting granule (SSG) detector: 0.45 kg of Sn granules (mean diameters 27.7 and 36.6 um, 10% volume filling in Teflon powder) in 56 pick-up coils at a base temperature of 115 mK; a WIMP recoil heats a granule above its superheated state and the lost Meissner effect is read as a flux change. Shielding of 15 cm lead, 4 cm copper and 18 cm borated polyethylene plus a plastic-scintillator muon veto at 70 m.w.e. Runs of two months (2002) and three weeks (2003); the paper derives a 90% C.L. spin-independent exclusion plot, lying above those of other experiments because of the relatively high background.
